title: Kenyan Pizza
community: Urban Kenya — the Nairobi pizza scene
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Pizza — thin-crust pizza topped with a spiced tomato and onion sauce, Kenyan spiced minced beef or chicken tikka, fresh kachumbari, avocado, and mozzarella. The Nairobi pizza — a global format with unmistakably Kenyan toppings.
longDesc: Nairobi has a thriving pizza scene, and the most popular Kenyan versions confidently put local ingredients on the pizza without apology — spiced beef, kachumbari, avocado, and pili pili drizzle transform the Italian format into something entirely Kenyan.
ingredients: 2 tbsp pili pili sauce — for drizzle
steps: Make dough: mix yeast, sugar, and warm water. Rest 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour and salt. Add yeast mixture and olive oil. Knead 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and rest 1 hour until doubled.
Make sauce: cook onion, garlic, tomatoes, and spices until thick — 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 250°C with baking tray inside.
Roll dough thinly to desired size.
Spread sauce, top with cheese and spiced beef.
Bake 10—12 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbling.
Remove from oven. Add kachumbari, avocado, pili pili drizzle, and coriander.
chefTips: Preheating the baking tray creates a crispy base.
Add kachumbari and avocado after baking — fresh toppings after the oven.
A very hot oven (250°C) is essential for pizza.
commonMistakes: Too many toppings — overloaded pizza does not cook evenly.
cookingScience: Preheating the baking tray simulates a pizza stone — the immediate contact with the hot surface drives rapid moisture evaporation from the base, creating the characteristic crispy crust.
sustainabilityTips: Local Kenyan toppings — avocado, kachumbari, local beef — make this pizza sustainably Kenyan.
culturalNote: Kenyan pizza with avocado, kachumbari, and spiced beef represents the confidence of Nairobi's modern food culture — a global format claimed and transformed into something unmistakably local.
